article_descriptions.screen-free-nature-activities.html:
Try this free mission today: choose five colours and ask your child to spot a natural example of each on a short walk. Look closely, leave plants where they grow, and finish with: ‘Which colour surprised you?’

The full guide has seven simple activities for ages 6–11, plus a link to the GSA Starter Kit when you’re ready for a complete printable adventure.
article_descriptions.screen-free-ocean-activities-for-kids.ht:
Bring a little ocean curiosity to your next family afternoon. Explore our free guide to screen-free ocean activities for children aged 6–11, with ideas for home or the coast.

Ready for a complete printable secret-agent adventure? Follow the guide’s link to the GSA Starter Kit to see what’s included.
article_descriptions.why-we-make-kids-the-agents.html:
Give a child a small role today: ‘You’re our nature detective. Find one thing outside that you didn’t notice yesterday.’ Let them sketch it and report back.

Gaia’s Secret Agents combines stories, observation and achievable real-world action. Read why we use this approach, with links to the research and our printable Starter Kit.
article_descriptions.sustainability-activities-primary-school:
Try this with a class or homeschooler: choose one familiar school or home routine, observe what actually happens, then compare two realistic ways it could work better. Ask students to justify the change with evidence rather than slogans.

The full free guide has nine low-prep sustainability activities for ages 6–11, with systems thinking, biodiversity, water, resource choices and practical action.

featured_pages.title: What if the best 10 minutes of the day cost A$5?
featured_pages.description:
Not another worksheet. Not another screen.

The Secret Meeting Cards are a little ritual for connection: sit together, draw a card, talk, imagine or act. Kids can lead. Grown-ups join in. Anyone can pass. One round takes about 10–20 minutes.

The Founding Pack has 16 cards plus the meeting guide, action sheet and printable storage box. A$5 instant PDF for ages 6–11.

It is really about the bit you get for free: laughing, listening, surprising each other and doing something together.

featured_pages.title: A family activity that doesn’t really feel like an activity
featured_pages.description:
Try this tonight: put the phones away, sit together and let one person draw a Secret Meeting card.

Everyone gets a turn. There are no wrong answers. Anyone can pass. Grown-ups play too.

TALK • IMAGINE • DO.

Then finish with one tiny Earth mission.

The full Founding Pack is A$5 and includes 16 printable cards, a meeting guide, action sheet and storage box.

featured_pages.title: For siblings. Parents. Grandparents. Kids.
featured_pages.description:
The Secret Meeting isn’t really about the cards. The cards are the excuse to sit down together.

Ask a strange question. Tell a story. Act like an animal. Imagine another world. Decide what your family could do to help one small piece of the real one.

Ages 6–11, but the grown-ups join in too. One round takes about 10 minutes. A$5 instant printable Founding Pack.

featured_pages.title: Make connection the activity.
featured_pages.description:
You do not need a big plan for family time. Choose a card. Ask the question. Listen to the answer. Laugh when the answer is weird. Let the kids surprise you.

The Secret Meeting Cards turn 10–20 minutes into a small family ritual: TALK, IMAGINE, DO — then choose one tiny Earth mission together.

16 printable cards plus guide, action sheet and tuck box. A$5 instant PDF.

featured_pages.title: Go slow. Spot more. Your family’s tiny-world mission.
featured_pages.description:
An Earth Protector mission doesn’t need a big outing.

Try the Tiny World Hunt together: look for five small wonders outside — a seed, a fallen leaf, a feather, an insect or a patch of moss. Choose one, sketch it, then describe it without naming it. Can the rest of the family guess?

Everyone gets to be the expert for a moment, including the grown-ups. Observe wildlife gently and leave living things where you found them.

Find four free, screen-free mini nature missions at Gaia’s Secret Agents. The activities can be read online without signing up; a separate email option is available for more missions.

featured_pages.title: Agent Kai’s backyard ocean mission: find a safe route
featured_pages.description:
Can your family guide a sea turtle through an ocean adventure — without leaving the backyard?

Kai, our wise green sea turtle and Ocean Guide, has a challenge for the whole crew. Pretend your backyard or local park is an ocean map. Choose a “feeding ground” and a “nesting beach”, then place three safe obstacles between them. One agent tries to find a route without touching an obstacle. Swap roles and try again with a partner giving directions.

Now the big question: what might make a real sea turtle’s journey difficult, and how can people help protect its habitat?

It’s screen-free family play with movement, imagination and a little ocean curiosity. No printing or email sign-up is needed to read the free activity guide.

featured_pages.title: The tree that could talk: tonight’s family Secret Meeting
featured_pages.description:
If the oldest tree in your street could tell your family one secret, what would it say?

Try a little Secret Meeting tonight. Ask everyone that question, then listen. The youngest might invent a dragon. A grandparent might remember what the neighbourhood looked like years ago. Every answer counts, and anyone can pass.

Finish by choosing one tiny Earth Protector action together — perhaps caring for a pot plant or leaving a little corner of the garden for wildlife.

That’s the spirit of Gaia’s Secret Agents Secret Meeting Cards: 16 printable TALK, IMAGINE and DO prompts to help children and grown-ups laugh, connect and care for nature. The Founding Pack is a digital A4 PDF to download and print at home; no physical cards are posted.

Secret Headquarters has a mission for the whole family. Make an Agent name, step outside together and follow the 15-minute Nature Signal Hunt. Let your young Earth Protector lead the investigation while the grown-ups follow their clues.

featured_pages.title: Secret Headquarters challenge: make a nature sound map
featured_pages.description:
Could your family draw a map using only your ears?

Secret Headquarters has a new challenge for curious Earth Protectors: the Nature Sound Map.

Find a safe spot outdoors. Close your eyes for 30 seconds and listen. Can you hear birds, rustling leaves, insects or footsteps? Draw a dot for where you're sitting, then add a mark in the direction of each sound. Compare maps — did the kids notice something the grown-ups missed?

It's a simple, screen-free way to practise observation and enjoy a little family time. No special equipment, no need to collect wildlife, and no perfect answers.

Our free guide has 10 environmental activities for kids aged 6–11, including the Nature Sound Map, pollinator watching and bird investigations. Read the activities online; no email or printing required.
